Original source account: The Riemann problem introduced on printed page 5 consists of a hyperbolic equation with constant left and right initial states separated by a single jump at x = 0, with no initial value specified at the interface itself (equation (1.11)). The selected sentence on printed page 8 extends this setup to include a discontinuity in the medium at that same interface. Material-parameter jumps provide the surrounding physical context (printed page 7, Section 1.4). The selected passage does not define a topology or a precise material profile, and its subsequent discussion of wave decomposition, reflection, and transmission is a separate claim (printed page 8, first paragraph).
assumptions: The inherited Riemann setup consists of a hyperbolic equation and piecewise constant initial data with a single jump at x = 0 [printed page 5, Section 1.2.1, opening paragraph and equation (1.11)].
In the extended setup, the medium also has a discontinuity at x = 0 [printed page 8, Section 1.4, selected sentence].
The selected discussion concerns linear waves in heterogeneous media, within Section 1.4, 'Linear Waves and Discontinuous Media' [printed pages 7–8, section heading and surrounding paragraphs].
Finite volume cells can carry different averaged material properties, motivating Riemann problems at interfaces between cells [printed page 8, Section 1.4, first paragraph].
Conservation form is not a standing requirement of the surrounding variable-coefficient discussion [printed page 8, Section 1.4, second paragraph].

Coordinator-selected interpretation: Use distinct one-sided local material traces at the same interface as distinct initial-state traces. Retain two constant strict-half-line initial states without requiring the material itself to be globally constant on each half-line.
